questions.question: display: grid on a container makes its direct children:

options.text: Grid items laid out along defined rows and columns

questions.explanation: grid establishes a grid formatting context; direct children become grid items placed into the implicit/explicit tracks.

questions.question: grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr 1fr creates:

options.text: Three columns where the middle takes twice the free space of the outer two

questions.explanation: fr units share leftover space proportionally: 2fr gets double the 1fr columns' share.

questions.question: The 'implicit grid' is created when:

options.text: Items are placed beyond the explicitly defined rows/columns

questions.explanation: Explicit tracks come from template-*; auto-placed items that overflow generate implicit rows/columns (sized by grid-auto-rows/columns).

questions.question: To make a 12-column layout where an item spans columns 2-9, use:
questions.explanation: grid-column: start / end uses line numbers (end is exclusive). 2/10 spans lines 2 through 9 = 7 columns.

questions.question: grid-auto-flow: dense helps by:

options.text: Backfilling earlier gaps with smaller items to reduce holes

questions.explanation: dense packing reorders auto-placement to fill gaps, producing a tighter layout (at the cost of source order).

questions.question: minmax(100px, 1fr) as a track size means:

options.text: At least 100px, but can grow to fill 1fr of free space

questions.explanation: minmax(min, max) sets a flexible range — min(100px) ensures a floor, 1fr lets it expand.

questions.question: place-items: center centers:

options.text: Each grid item within its OWN cell (shorthand for justify/align-items)
The whole grid in the page

questions.explanation: place-items sets both align-items and justify-items, centering content inside each cell — handy for card centers.

questions.question: Subgrid (modern CSS) allows a grid item to:

options.text: Align its OWN children to the parent grid's tracks

questions.explanation: Subgrid lets a nested grid inherit the parent's row/column lines so inner content aligns to the outer layout — great for cards.
